text:
alice.prod: Heads up — multiple hosted-inference customers are reporting a sudden spike in 502/504 gateway errors and long tail latencies from us-east-2 (AZ2). Some requests succeed on retry, others fail consistently. Example repro: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' -> 502 after ~12s. Seeing token auth retries for a subset. Anyone else seeing this?

ben.net: I'm seeing a simultaneous spike in TCP retransmits and duplicate ACKs on the egress path from edge-us-east-2 to transit ASN 64512 starting ~03:02 UTC. Preliminary note: BGP session flapped with neighbor 203.0.113.45, routes oscillating between peer-A and peer-B. Pulling pcap and traceroutes now.

csm_jay: Customer on the line, they report ~30% failure rate for inference calls over the last 10 minutes. Asking for ETA and any immediate mitigations/fallbacks — can we failover them to another region or Dedicated capacity quickly?

oncall_network: Oncall-network here. Escalating to provider NOC (ticket #NOC-8942). Temporarily enabling route dampening and pinning to peer-B to reduce flaps. Also creating a short-term routing policy to prefer alternate peer for edge-us-east-2 prefixes. Will post changes once applied.

deploy-bot: Deploy rollback: edge-gateway-1 rollback triggered (CI-3201) — rollback performed at 03:15 UTC due to elevated 5xxs.

nina-sre: From service logs: most 502s surface at the edge gateway with message "upstream timed out" — backend inference nodes report normal CPU/GPU utilization but elevated connection resets from upstream. Suggests network egress instability rather than application-level overload. I'm starting tcpdump on gateway-1 (interface eth0) and collecting per-connection RTT histograms.

ben.net: Pasted traceroute and tcpdump snippets below (sanitized).

```
# traceroute to 198.51.100.10 (inference pool)
traceroute to 198.51.100.10, 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  edge-us-east-2 (10.10.1.1)  0.45 ms  0.41 ms  0.39 ms
 2  peer-A (198.51.100.1)     1.12 ms  1.10 ms  1.15 ms
 3  198.51.101.5 (transit)     20.4 ms  20.2 ms  45.1 ms  <-- route flip seen here
 4  198.51.100.10             21.3 ms  48.7 ms  21.5 ms

# tcpdump snippet: repeated dup ACKs and retransmits
12:03:05.123456 IP 10.10.1.2.443 > 10.20.3.4.52344: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0, length 0
12:03:05.123789 IP 10.10.1.2.443 > 10.20.3.4.52344: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0, length 0
12:03:05.124012 IP 10.20.3.4.52344 > 10.10.1.2.443: Flags [DUP ACK] ack 12345
12:03:05.124300 IP 10.20.3.4.52344 > 10.10.1.2.443: Flags [RST]
```

ben.net: Observations: path alternates between 20ms and 45ms RTT indicating oscillation between two transit paths. Also seeing signs of PMTU issues (ICMP fragmentation needed observed intermittently) which can cause tail latency and retransmits on some flows.

mike-support: Also getting customer reports about doubled billing footprints because their client retried automatically; please flag impacted request_ids so billing can consider credits. I've opened billing ticket BILL-2073.

oncall_network: Provider NOC confirms partial flap on the interconnect fabric. They've isolated a misbehaving port on peer-A and plan a hardware bypass. Meanwhile we applied route pinning to peer-B at 03:22 UTC. Mitigation steps: 1) prefer peer-B for 15m; 2) increase edge gateway upstream timeout to absorb transient retransmits; 3) enable graceful degrade to cached /response for small inference calls where applicable.

alice.prod: Can we draft a customer-facing status message and a post-incident timeline? CSMs need ETA. Also we should add impacted request prefixes to a billing hold list until postmortem.

nina-sre: Quick metrics update: error rate (5xx) for hosted inference in us-east-2 dropped from 28% -> ~3% after the route pin at 03:22 UTC. Latency p95 improved but p99 still elevated for some flows (likely PMTU or intermittent blackhole). Continuing capture for next 30–60m.

csm_jay: Relayed to customer: we'll credit affected requests and share incident timeline once we have full postmortem. They're satisfied with the interim mitigation.

oncall_network: Leaving this thread open for follow-ups from provider NOC and SRE. Provider to confirm repair and BGP stability in next 30 minutes. If stable, we'll remove dampening and revert to normal peer preferences.

nina-sre: Action items captured: SRE to collect full pcaps + BGP updates, Network to confirm BGP session stability, Support to collate impacted request ids for billing, Product to publish status update. Will own postmortem template.

mike-support: Noted. I'll start compiling affected request ids and customer call notes.

alice.prod: Thanks everyone — marking severity P1 and will follow up on postmortem.
